title: SFINAE (Substitution Failure Is Not An Error) & std::enable_if

slides.title: SFINAE Principle
slides.prompt: SFINAE dictates that if an invalid type/expression is created during template argument substitution, the compiler discards that overload instead of raising a compile error.

slides.title: SFINAE Acronym
slides.prompt: SFINAE stands for Substitution Failure Is Not An ___.
slides.codeSnippet:
// SFINAE definition:
Substitution Failure Is Not An ___

slides.title: std::enable_if Purpose
slides.prompt: What is the primary usage of 'std::enable_if' in template metaprogramming?
options: Conditionally enable/disable template overloads based on compile-time boolean traits
Enable runtime exception handling for templates
Force template instantiation on the heap
slides.correctAnswer: Conditionally enable/disable template overloads based on compile-time boolean traits

slides.title: SFINAE Scope Limit
slides.prompt: Where must substitution errors occur for SFINAE to discard an overload gracefully?
options: In the immediate context of the function template signature (declaration/parameters/return type)
Inside the nested body of the function implementation
In any called sub-function anywhere in the program
slides.correctAnswer: In the immediate context of the function template signature (declaration/parameters/return type)

slides.title: SFINAE vs C++20 Concepts
slides.prompt: Why are C++20 Concepts preferred over pre-C++20 SFINAE enable_if techniques?
options: Concepts produce dramatically clearer compiler error messages and faster compile times
Concepts work at runtime while SFINAE works at compile time
Concepts completely eliminate the need for templates
SFINAE is deprecated and removed in C++20
slides.correctAnswer: Concepts produce dramatically clearer compiler error messages and faster compile times
